notVerified: Nothing was listened to; all verification is by numbers. The 8 ms fade-in softens the attack of hard hits (k_hit_*, k_land_*): their first millisecond peaks at about -27 to -42 dBFS because the ramp follows the source, so a measure of 'first millisecond above -60 dBFS' would still flag fade-in files; the first and last SAMPLE are the discontinuity and those are at most -80.8 dBFS. The last millisecond is below -66 dBFS everywhere.

The level table values for pairs that levels.py has no value for (engines short -8 peak, impacts long -26 LUFS, switches long -30, cabin short -16 peak, sensors short -16 peak, alarms/drive/weapons rows) are my estimates, commented in build.py. Whether the downloads now sit right against the rendered sounds was only checked numerically.
The full render of all sounds was not run (only --manifest-only), as instructed. The manifest count 110 includes pilot sounds other agents had rendered at that moment and will change.
The synth test run happened while other agents were writing synth/cat_pilot_*.py; it passed then.
The NASA entries left were not listened to for hidden voices.
notes: Clipping rule deviation, on purpose: the literal rule (within 0.1 % of the file maximum) found nothing in n_sls_test_fire because the mp3 decode overshoots up to 1.14 and the flat plateaus sit at 1.0. build.py therefore takes magnitudes above full scale as full scale before applying the rule. This also means a loud clean LOW sine (200 Hz at 0.99) trips the rule (peak lasts 3 samples within 0.1 %); a test documents it. Source clipping is measured on the excerpt (what is used), after channel mix-down and before resampling.
Ceiling for the processed downloads is -1.05 dBFS true peak (not -1.00), so that dither and rounding to 16 bit never put a file above -1.
Excerpt of the whole file is not scanned for clipping: only the part used.

validate_manifest now also requires a spectrogram file for downloads, checks.centroidHz and checks.sourceClipped, duration > 0 and true peak <= -1 for downloads. assemble_manifest ignores any JSON under render/downloads/ (no sidecars are written there) and the build deletes processed copies in <out>/downloads of ids no longer in selection.json (the 15 struck copies were removed from assets/audio/render/downloads).

Old render/downloads copies had no hash relationship to the new ones: every download's hash changed, so the owner's ratings of downloads will show as changed in the audition page. ratings.json was not touched.

Struck: 30 downloads.json entries, not 31: every entry marked speech or probable (the brief's 15 selection entries plus 15 that were never selected: mercury6-god-speed, mercury4-clock-started, mercury7-liftoff/fireflies/guaymas, sts-houston-discovery-2, sts-wheelstop/computers-in-control/apu-shutdown, sts1-dust-it-off, apollo11-day03-highlights, artemis2-integrity-voice-check/good-burn/go-no-go-poll/closest-point). The notTaken entries have the form {what, why} with what = 'title (id, url)'.

Doubtful remaining NASA entries (marked none, I did not decide): nasa-mars-rover-driving ('90-second highlights', could carry a narration), nasa-sls-test-fire (test-fire recording, could carry launch-control chatter or countdown), nasa-mars-ingenuity-flight and nasa-mars-supercam-lasers/wind (rover recordings, unlikely). Quindar tones stay. n_rover_driving and n_sls_test_fire are the ones worth a listen.
Line endings: build.py is CRLF in the working tree and kept CRLF; the JSON files are written CRLF with indent 2 (same as before) so the git diff is only the removed entries.

Other files that may need a change by their owners: SOUND_DESIGN.md and docs mention the NASA speech selection (not touched). The audition page and anything reading manifest 'file' for downloads now get 'downloads/<id>.wav' (relative to the render folder) instead of '../downloads/...'.
